style="whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;aspect=fixed;fillColor=light-dark(#FFFFFF,#000000);fontColor=light-dark(#000000,#FF9999);" value="<div class="heading-wrapper"><h3 id="tier-0---identity-control-plane" class="heading-anchor">Tier 0 - Identity control plane</h3></div><br><p>Tier 0 contains assets and identities that directly or indirectly control the directory service and enterprise-wide permissions:</p><div align="left"><br><ul><li>Tier 0 administrative accounts and groups, including built-in Active<br> Directory groups such as Backup Operators and Server Operators.</li><li>AD DS domain controllers and core directory service components.</li><li>Identity services such as Microsoft Entra Connect, Microsoft Entra <br>application proxy, Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS), and <br>Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS).</li><li>Systems that operate or manage Tier 0 identity systems, including <br>backup, monitoring, patching, hypervisor, antivirus, and endpoint <br>detection and response (EDR) solutions, or any agent with direct <br>operating system-level or AD-object-level control.</li></ul></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="430" width="430" x="-190" y="-600" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="FPqMHxv_qP33vrG37nPg-115" parent="1" style="whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;aspect=fixed;fillColor=light-dark(#000000,#000000);fontColor=light-dark(#000000,#FAFFBA);" value="<div class="heading-wrapper"><h3 id="tier-1---enterprise-server-and-application-management" class="heading-anchor">Tier 1 - Enterprise server and application management</h3></div><br><p>Tier 1 contains member servers and the identities that manage them:</p><br><div align="left"><ul><li>Member servers and server administrator roles.</li><li>IT infrastructure management (ITIM) solutions that control Tier 1 servers.</li><li>Microsoft server applications such as Exchange Server, SharePoint Server, and SQL Server.</li><li>Third-party server solutions.</li><li>LOB applications.</li></ul></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="340" width="340" x="330" y="-600" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="FPqMHxv_qP33vrG37nPg-116" parent="1" style="whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;aspect=fixed;fontColor=light-dark(#000000,#97D077);" value="<div class="heading-wrapper"><h3 id="tier-2---end-user-account-and-device-support" class="heading-anchor">Tier 2 - End-user account and device support</h3></div><br><p align="left">Tier 2 contains the identities that manage end-user devices and <br>accounts, including help desk and device support roles, end-user device <br>administrator roles, and end-user account administrator roles.</p>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="284.6" width="284.6" x="760" y="-600" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="FPqMHxv_qP33vrG37nPg-117" parent="1" style="whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;aspect=fixed;" value="<div class="heading-wrapper"><h3 id="tier-model-design-principles" class="heading-anchor">Tier model design principles</h3></div><br><p>Apply these principles when you decide whether an asset, account, or solution belongs in a particular tier:</p><br><div align="left"><ul><li><strong>Least privilege within each tier.</strong> Even within Tier 0, not every account needs Domain Admins rights. Scope permissions to the minimum required for each role.</li><li><strong>No shared credentials across tiers.</strong> An account, <br>service account, or group must operate in a single tier. Reusing <br>credentials across tiers collapses the trust boundary.</li><li><strong>No line-of-business workloads in Tier 0.</strong> Application servers, business apps, and general-purpose workloads belong in Tier 1, even when an AD admin owns them.</li><li><strong>Separation of duties.</strong> Keep operators, approvers, <br>and auditors as distinct roles, especially in Tier 0. Avoid <br>concentrating all privileged functions in a single team.</li><li><strong>Containment, not perimeter, is the boundary.</strong> <br>Network segmentation supports the model but doesn't replace it. The <br>credential and the keyboard define the tier, not the IP address</li></ul></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="520" width="520" x="220" y="-1160" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell div.p: Tier 0 contains assets and identities that directly or indirectly control the directory service and enterprise-wide permissions:

ul.li:
Tier 0 administrative accounts and groups, including built-in Active
Directory groups such as Backup Operators and Server Operators.
AD DS domain controllers and core directory service components.

Identity services such as Microsoft Entra Connect, Microsoft Entra
application proxy, Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS), and
Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS).

Systems that operate or manage Tier 0 identity systems, including
backup, monitoring, patching, hypervisor, antivirus, and endpoint
detection and response (EDR) solutions, or any agent with direct
operating system-level or AD-object-level control.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 338px; height: 1px; padding-top: 730px; margin-left: 731px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #FAFFBA); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.h3: Tier 1 - Enterprise server and application management

div.p: Tier 1 contains member servers and the identities that manage them:

ul.li: Member servers and server administrator roles.
IT infrastructure management (ITIM) solutions that control Tier 1 servers.
Microsoft server applications such as Exchange Server, SharePoint Server, and SQL Server.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 283px; height: 1px; padding-top: 703px; margin-left: 1161px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #97D077); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.h3: Tier 2 - End-user account and device support

div.p:
Tier 2 contains the identities that manage end-user devices and
accounts, including help desk and device support roles, end-user device
administrator roles, and end-user account administrator roles.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 518px; height: 1px; padding-top: 260px; margin-left: 621px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.p: Apply these principles when you decide whether an asset, account, or solution belongs in a particular tier:

ul.li: Least privilege within each tier. Even within Tier 0, not every account needs Domain Admins rights. Scope permissions to the minimum required for each role.

No shared credentials across tiers. An account,
service account, or group must operate in a single tier. Reusing
credentials across tiers collapses the trust boundary.
No line-of-business workloads in Tier 0. Application servers, business apps, and general-purpose workloads belong in Tier 1, even when an AD admin owns them.

Separation of duties. Keep operators, approvers,
and auditors as distinct roles, especially in Tier 0. Avoid
concentrating all privileged functions in a single team.

Containment, not perimeter, is the boundary.
Network segmentation supports the model but doesn't replace it. The
credential and the keyboard define the tier, not the IP address
